rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Columbia was the command module of the command and service module, which was built by North American Aviation [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". North American Aviation was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

Answer: North American Aviation.

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The investigating board, the Apollo 13 Review Board chaired by Edgar Cortright, said the explosion was an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report also called the switch failure a serious oversight shared by all parties. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not state, in a fact line, that the board named the thermostatic switches as the cause of the fire, so I cannot give that link as sourced.

rows.question: How long before Kennedy's speech at Rice University did NASA announce its Apollo mission mode?
rows.answer:
NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". Kennedy gave the Rice University speech on 1962-09-12 [[john-f-kennedy]] "[stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The announcement came 63 days before the speech.

rows.question: Which Apollo 11 crew member earned a doctorate on the kind of rendezvous Apollo relied on, and in which year?
rows.answer: Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 lunar module pilot, earned his MIT doctorate in 1963. His thesis was on manned orbital rendezvous [[buzz-aldrin]] "- [stated] Earned an MIT doctorate in 1963 with a thesis on manned orbital rendezvous (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". Apollo relied on lunar orbit rendezvous, the mission mode NASA chose in 1962, which needed a separate lander [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "- [stated] Required a separate lander, which became the lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The notes do not state that his thesis was specifically on lunar orbit rendezvous, only on manned orbital rendezvous.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

His exposure set off the crew swap, which put Jack Swigert on Apollo 13 in place of Ken Mattingly. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives, but he died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

The brain doesn't say when or how he died.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank was oxygen tank No. 2, and it was carried by the command and service module. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The command and service module carried it: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins, the command module pilot. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

During the landing, he stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised adapter made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide CO2 canisters were square and the lunar module's sockets were round. Engineers devised the adapter, and the crew built it from radioed instructions.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?
rows.answer:
The Cortright report, the *Report of the Apollo 13 Review Board* (June 1970), described the switch failure as a shared oversight. Press coverage from 1970 reported that it "called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share" [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)". The notes give this only through that 1970 coverage, not the report's own wording.

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)".

The tank's thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". The notes do not explicitly say that the switches failed under 65-volt power, so I have not stated it as a finding.

The board recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
The checker compared against the full fact lines, which begin with the `[stated]` tag. I dropped that tag before, so the quotes failed. The corrected citations below include it.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. Mission Control's abort decision changed the goal from a Fra Mauro lunar landing to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"; [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down, having used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Cortright Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. The day is not recorded. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The report's content is that the switch failure was a serious oversight that all parties share. That line is cited to Michigan Daily coverage, not to a date, so I've left it out of the dated list.
